algorithm.rul: LightGBM gradient-boosted trees (L2 loss), RUL target capped at 125 cycles
algorithm.interval: 80% split-conformal interval, calibrated per band of predicted RUL on validation engines within 150 cycles of failure
algorithm.failure: LightGBM binary classifier for failure within 30 cycles
algorithm.explanations: Exact TreeSHAP contributions of the RUL model, summed per sensor

training_data.source: NASA C-MAPSS turbofan degradation simulation (Saxena et al., 2008)

feature_description: Each sensor is converted to a z-score against the healthy early-life baseline of its operating regime (6 regimes from altitude, Mach and throttle). Per sensor: 10- and 30-cycle rolling means, 20-cycle trend slope, and drift from the engine's own first recorded cycles. Plus cycles in service.

previous_release.name: v2.0.0 LSTM (FD001 only)
previous_release.note: The v2 API repeated one reading 30 times instead of using the engine's history.

limitations: Trained on simulated data (C-MAPSS). Real engines need retraining on their own run-to-failure records.
The RUL target is capped at 125 cycles, so early-life engines all read as '125+'.
Drift is measured from the first recorded cycles. Histories that start mid-life hide earlier wear.
Only degradation modes present in the training data (HPC and fan) are represented.
